issues.legal_issue: Landowners whose acquired land is comparable to land acquired earlier are entitled to a notional increase in market value for the intervening period.
material_facts: The landowners appealed the compensation fixed for their acquired land.
The acquired land was undisputedly similar to land for which compensation had previously been assessed.
The comparable land had been acquired earlier than the land at issue.
The High Court fixed compensation by reference to the earlier assessment but did not allow an increase for the intervening period.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, and the landowners were held entitled to compensation at Rs.49 per square yard, reflecting a 12% per annum increase rounded off. The acquiring authority was directed to pay the enhanced compensation with statutory benefits.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the principle of notional increase in market value where comparable land was acquired earlier, the Court held that an annual increase should be allowed for the period between the comparable acquisition and the acquisition at issue. It relied on Ranjit Singh v. U.T. of Chandigarh (1992) 4 SCC 659, Land Acquisition Officer v. Ramanjulu (2005) 9 SCC 594, Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti v. Bipin Kumar (2004) 2 SCC 283, Sardar Jogendra Singh v. State of U.P. (2008) 17 SCC 133, Revenue Divl. Officer-cum-LAO v. Sk. Azam Saheb (2009) 4 SCC 395, ONGC Ltd. v. Rameshbhai Jivanbhai Patel (2008) 14 SCC 745, and Valliyammal v. Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition) (2011) 8 SCC 91. The acquisition was referred under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; the judgment does not rely on that provision as the basis for the notional increase.

rule.if: land_compensation_appeal and comparable_land_is_similar and comparable_land_acquired_earlier and later_acquisition_at_issue

predicates.land_compensation_appeal: Landowners brought an appeal concerning the compensation awarded for acquired land.
predicates.comparable_land_is_similar: The parties did not dispute that the acquired land was similar to land used as a compensation comparator.
predicates.comparable_land_acquired_earlier: The land used as a comparator had been acquired before the land at issue.
predicates.later_acquisition_at_issue: The landowners' land was acquired after the comparable land.

issues.definition: When landowners appeal compensation for land similar to land acquired earlier, and their own land was acquired later, they are entitled to a notional increase in compensation.
